security_audit.summary: Markdown backticks and multilingual prose explain the execution and entropy alerts; the government URLs support the stated public-data workflow. Predictable temporary paths permit local symlink attacks and unintended overwrites during download and extraction. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The download writes to a predictable shared temporary filename.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private directory with mktemp -d and store the archive there; avoid privileged execution and remove the directory after use.

remediation.issue: Archive extraction overwrites files in a predictable shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Extract into the new private directory without forced overwrites; reject archive entries with absolute paths, traversal components, or symbolic links.

content.value_statement: Taiwan property records require careful handling of quarterly files, date formats, and price units. This skill guides government CSV downloads and contextual transaction reporting.
actual_capabilities: Provides the government quarterly ZIP download command without requiring an API key or login.
Explains county file selection for sales, presales, and rentals.
Documents UTF-8 BOM encoding, dual CSV headers, and transaction field meanings.
Provides a Python example for filtering Zhongshan District property transactions and printing prices.
Explains ROC season codes and conversion from price per square meter to price per ping.
Directs reports to include the data quarter, reporting delays, masked addresses, and special transaction caveats.
limitations: Quarterly registry data does not provide live listings, pending negotiations, or guaranteed coverage of recent transactions.
Execution requires network access, curl, unzip, and Python for the supplied parsing example.
Masked addresses and special transactions limit precise property comparisons.
The Python example retains the English header and does not implement sorting; verify parsing and ordering before relying on results.

use_cases.title: Review Neighborhood Transactions
use_cases.description: Inspect reported sales for a district and understand price units, reporting delays, and unusual transaction remarks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Quarterly Market Comparisons
use_cases.description: Use county sales, presale, and rental files to support comparisons with clearly stated periods and exclusions.

use_cases.title: Check Property Reporting Evidence
use_cases.description: Locate government transaction records and describe source limitations without inferring exact masked addresses.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Available Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which quarterly Taiwan property files cover sales, presales, and rentals. Describe the reporting delay and address masking.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a County Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve Taipei sales data for 2026 Q2 using a private temporary directory. Confirm the county file and report the source quarter.

prompt_templates.title: Compare District Prices
prompt_templates.prompt: Filter Zhongshan District property sales for 2026 Q2. Exclude special transactions, sort by unit price, and show TWD per square meter and ping.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Quarterly Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two available quarters for Taipei sales. Validate both CSV headers, county codes, transaction categories, missing values, and special remarks before summarizing differences.

output_examples.input: Show an example of a properly qualified transaction report.
output_examples.output: Illustrative report from the skill: 2026 Q2 data includes a Zhongshan parking-space transaction dated June 1 for TWD 3.7 million. Registry declarations typically lag transactions by one to two months. This is the documented example, not a fresh lookup.

output_examples.input: Convert TWD 200,000 per square meter into a price per ping.
output_examples.output: TWD 200,000 per square meter equals TWD 661,158 per ping, using the documented factor of 3.30579. This illustrative conversion does not establish a property valuation.

output_examples.input: Why are transactions from last week missing?
output_examples.output: Quarterly files and declaration delays can exclude recent transactions. Check the available quarter and allow for the documented one-to-two-month lag. Missing records do not prove that no transactions occurred.

best_practices: Download and extract data in a newly created private temporary directory without elevated privileges.
Validate both header rows and field positions, then explicitly sort results when ordering matters.
State the quarter, price units, reporting delay, and treatment of special transactions in every comparison.
anti_patterns: Treating quarterly declaration records as live market prices or pending deal information.
Inferring exact property addresses from masked address ranges.
Mixing parking spaces, land, and property sales without category checks or special transaction review.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or account?
faq.answer: The documented government quarterly download requires neither an API key nor a login.

faq.question: Which transaction types are covered?
faq.answer: County files use suffix a for sales, b for presales, and c for rentals.

faq.question: Can I query live or pending transactions?
faq.answer: No. The workflow uses quarterly declared records and does not cover pending negotiations or live individual queries.

faq.question: How are prices converted to ping?
faq.answer: Multiply the price per square meter by 3.30579 to obtain the price per ping.

faq.question: What if the requested quarter is unavailable?
faq.answer: Try the preceding quarter and state which quarter was actually retrieved.

faq.question: Can the supplied commands run unchanged?
faq.answer: Use private temporary paths first. Correct the CSV header handling and add explicit sorting when needed; do not assume the example sorts results.
